prose: Anil Dash, quoted in The Guardian, makes the case for 'lots of little indie AIs' rather than a ChatGPT killer: many small, responsible players instead of a few giants - mammals after the comet. He frames this against a charged backdrop: Trump administration AI policymakers suspended access to Anthropic's newest product, and Dash notes those policymakers hold webs of investments in competing players (including the about-to-IPO SpaceX), making honest risk judgment impossible.

He also points to the cultural pushback against AI - strongest among people born this century - while usage data shows even younger cohorts use some AI tools, a pattern he compares to social media's trajectory.
highlights: Dash in The Guardian: the alternative is many little responsible AI players, not one ChatGPT killer
Trump administration AI policymakers suspended access to Anthropic's newest product
Dash cites policymakers' conflicts of interest, including investments in SpaceX ahead of its IPO
Anti-AI sentiment is strongest among those born this century, yet they still use some AI tools
He compares AI adoption patterns to the earlier arc of social media
